name: New Forms
editorial_article: "New Forms" (1997) is the landmark debut studio album by the British drum and bass collective Roni Size & Reprazent. Emerging from the Bristol music scene—a hotbed for the fusion of breakbeat culture, jazz, and dub—the album played a pivotal role in bringing drum and bass out of the underground rave scene and into the mainstream consciousness. Released via the seminal imprint Talkin' Loud, it was widely praised for its sophisticated fusion of live instrumentation with the frenetic, programmed breakbeats characteristic of jungle. By blending the organic textures of upright bass and jazz-inflected rhythms with electronic production, Roni Size, Krust, DJ Die, and Suv created a "jazzstep" blueprint that pushed the boundaries of the genre.\n\nThe album's impact was immediate, securing the 1997 Mercury Prize, a significant milestone for an electronic act at the time. With its expansive, ambitious structure—often spread across double-disc sets in its original CD release—"New Forms" offered a listening experience that was as suited for home listening as it was for the dancefloor. Featuring the soulful, atmospheric vocals of Onallee, tracks like "Brown Paper Bag" and "Watching Windows" became quintessential anthems, bridging the gap between high-energy club music and sophisticated, listenable production. Decades later, "New Forms" remains a defining text of 1990s electronic music, lauded for its production clarity, ambitious scope, and its successful mission to diversify the rhythmic palette of drum and bass. Its enduring influence is felt in the myriad ways producers have subsequently sought to incorporate live musicianship into the digital soundscapes of the breakbeat continuum.
